intro.text: Vic's Diner. Lenny has ordered the tuna on rye here every day for six years. This morning, Vic put the counter on the internet.
I talk to the counter through a computer? What do I say? Do I say please? Does it know me?
intro.say: [bewildered] I talk to the counter through a computer? What do I say? Do I say please? Does it know me?

intro.text: You send a request: a method, what to do, and a path, what to. It answers with a status. That's HTTP. And no, it doesn't know you.
The new kid makes the slips. Lenny once spent forty minutes arguing with a vending machine. He lost.

brief.text: Ask the counter for the menu. The whole menu. I'm not getting the tuna today. I'm a different man.
brief.say: [determined] Ask the counter for the menu. The whole menu. I'm not getting the tuna today. I'm a different man.

scenes.hint: GET means "give me". The path says what: the menu is at /menu.

after.text: Coffee. Toast. Tuna on rye. Cherry pie. Too many options. I'm going to need a minute.
after.say: [overwhelmed] Coffee. Toast. Tuna on rye. Cherry pie. Too many options. I'm going to need a minute.

brief.text: What did table 4 order? It's order number 7. Just that one. I don't need the life story of every sandwich in the place.

scenes.hint: One order has a path of its own: the collection's path, then its id.

after.text: Tuna on rye, table 4. That's your table, Lenny. You ordered the tuna before you sat down.
after.say: [deadpan] Tuna on rye, table 4. That's your table, Lenny. You ordered the tuna before you sat down.

brief.text: Lenny wants a toast at table 4. Put the order in, as JSON, before he loses his nerve.

scenes.hint: POST to the collection makes a new order in it. The body says what, and Content-Type says it's JSON.

after.text: Order 9! Toast! Look at me! Six years of tuna, and now I'm a toast guy!
after.say: [giddy] Order nine! Toast! Look at me! Six years of tuna, and now I'm a toast guy!

brief.text: I don't want to order. I want to know what a man is allowed to DO to order 7. All my options!
brief.say: [bursting in] I don't want to order. I want to know what a man is allowed to DO to order seven. All my options!

scenes.hint: There's a method for asking which methods a path takes. Its answer is in the Allow header.

after.text: PUT! PATCH! DELETE! Oh, the things I could do to that sandwich!
after.say: [thrilled] Put! Patch! Delete! Oh, the things I could do to that sandwich!

outro.text: 200, 201, 204. Anything starting with a 2 means it worked.
Their fault. Good luck getting them to admit it.
I'm going to live in the fives.
outro.say: [wistful] I'm going to live in the fives.

intro.text: A broth counter on 55th Street. A line round the block, a man behind it with rules, and no chairs. Chairs encourage chat.
Know what you want. Say it in JSON. Step up, don't chat. Get one thing wrong and he says one word.
His counter's an API. Every rule is a header or the body. Get one wrong, and you're back at the end of the line with the tourists.

brief.text: First, what's he got today? Lenny swears you have to say you'll take it as HTML. Lenny also swears he went to Yale.

scenes.hint: Accept is optional. Leave it off, or ask for something the counter has: it only does JSON.

after.text: Fine, no HTML. But I did go to Yale. For the tour.
after.say: [defensive] Fine, no HTML. But I did go to Yale. [beat] For the tour.

brief.text: The mulligatawny, a cup. And tell him the body's JSON. I'm not getting thrown out in front of the tourists again.
brief.say: [nervous] The mulligatawny, a cup. And tell him the body's JSON. I'm not getting thrown out in front of the tourists again.

scenes.hint: The body is JSON, so Content-Type says application/json. Anything else gets a 415.

after.text: 201! He took it! He didn't look at me, but he took it!
after.say: [whispering, thrilled] Two oh one! He took it! He didn't look at me, but he took it!

brief.text: My turn. Lobster bisque, a bowl. Every field he asks for, and not one he didn't. Lenny asked for bread once. We don't talk about it.

scenes.hint: An order here is a broth and a size. Leave one out, or add bread, and it's a 400.

brief.text: I wrote three slips for a cup of lentil! Only one of them is real JSON. I don't know which. That's the thrill!
brief.say: [breathless, excited] I wrote three slips for a cup of lentil! Only one of them is real JSON. I don't know which. That's the thrill!

scenes.hint: In JSON every key is a string, and strings take double quotes. Not single ones, not none.

after.text: Double quotes! Every key! I've been single-quoting my whole life like an animal!
after.say: [shocked] Double quotes! Every key! I've been single-quoting my whole life like an animal!

outro.text: He said it to your Content-Type.

intro.text: Saturday night at the Jade Lantern. Lenny booked a table. Then, to be safe, he booked another one. Then he lay awake wondering if they knew.
POST makes one! So I posted twice! If one table falls through, I've got a backup table!
intro.say: [proud] POST makes one! So I posted twice! If one table falls through, I've got a backup table!

intro.text: POST makes a new one every time. To change one you've got, PUT or PATCH it. To get rid of one, DELETE. To end up with two, be you.

brief.text: Make Kaplan's table, number 3, a table for four. Don't book a third one. He'll want to keep it for emergencies.

scenes.hint: PUT replaces the whole booking at its own path, so the body has all of it: the name and the size.

brief.text: Zelnick's bringing a date, and she's bringing a date. Make table 3 a six, and change nothing else.

scenes.hint: PATCH changes only the fields you send. PUT wants all of them.

brief.text: Table 4's the spare. Get rid of it before they charge me for it. Quietly. The man at the door is looking at me.
brief.say: [hushed, anxious] Table four's the spare. Get rid of it before they charge me for it. Quietly. The man at the door is looking at me.

scenes.hint: DELETE goes to the one thing you want gone, at its own path.

after.text: 204! No Content! No charge! It's like I was never here!
after.say: [relieved] Two oh four! No content! No charge! It's like I was never here!

brief.text: Is table 3 still ours? Don't read me the whole booking. I've heard enough about this booking for one lifetime. Yes or no.

scenes.hint: HEAD asks exactly what GET asks, and gets the status and headers back without the body.

outro.text: And did you see what DELETE sent back? 204. No Content. A response about nothing.
Finally, a status code about us.

intro.text: The post office on 81st Street, where Vernon has worked for eleven years and never once changed his mind, or his cardigan.
Every parcel has a version, Lerner. Ask if it's changed, I'll tell you. Change it without saying which version you saw, and I won't.
That's an ETag: a version stamp on a thing. You can ask for it only if it's changed. Or change it only if it hasn't.
He's waited eleven years for somebody to ask him that. Look at him. He's glowing.

brief.text: Has my mail changed since I last looked? I saw version 3. If not, Vernon needn't read it all out. He does voices.

scenes.hint: If-None-Match with the version you saw: if it's still that one, the answer is 304, and no body.

after.text: 304. Not Modified. Nothing new for you, Wexler. As usual.
after.say: [smug, savouring it] Three oh four. Not modified. Nothing new for you, Wexler. [beat] As usual.

brief.text: Send my resume to Mr. Pratt at the network. It says I'm fluent in HTTP. I'm conversational.

scenes.hint: A new parcel is a POST to the collection, with the body as JSON.

after.text: 202. Accepted. It'll get there when it gets there, Kaplan. Maybe Tuesday. Maybe never.
after.say: [smug] Two oh two. Accepted. It'll get there when it gets there, Kaplan. Maybe Tuesday. [beat] Maybe never.

brief.text: That parcel of Dana's is my birthday present. She'll keep it out of spite. Send it to me. Vernon wants the version: v2, on the board.
brief.say: That parcel of Dana's is my birthday present. She'll keep it out of spite. Send it to me. Vernon wants the version: v two, on the board.

scenes.hint: If-Match with the version on the board. Leave it off here and it's 428; an old one, 412.

after.text: That was a present, Stu. For my new boyfriend. Enjoy the cufflinks.
after.say: [icy] That was a present, Stu. For my new boyfriend. [beat] Enjoy the cufflinks.

brief.text: Kaplan wants his jury summons gone. Fine. Tell me which version, Kaplan. It's on the board. I'll wait. They pay me to wait.
brief.say: [slow, smug] Kaplan wants his jury summons gone. Fine. Tell me which version, Kaplan. It's on the board. I'll wait. They pay me to wait.

scenes.hint: DELETE the summons at its own path, with If-Match and the version the board shows for it.

after.text: Gone! No jury duty! Justice will have to manage without me!
after.say: [triumphant] Gone! No jury duty! Justice will have to manage without me!

outro.text: Version five, Lerner. It's been a pleasure.

intro.text: The network. A long table on the fortieth floor, and Mr. Pratt, who has never laughed. Not once. Not even at a wedding.
Our pilots are behind a login. Show me who you are, or don't come in.
I've got a pass! It's got my picture on it! I'm squinting, but it's me!
A token says who you are. 401 means it doesn't know you. 403 means it knows you, and the answer's no.

brief.text: Get the list of pilots. The door wants a token. Mine is stu-1990. The year I peaked.
brief.say: Get the list of pilots. The door wants a token. Mine is stu dash nineteen ninety. [dry] The year I peaked.

scenes.hint: Authorization: Bearer, then the token. A token it doesn't know is as good as none: 401.

brief.text: Send in my pilot, "Kaplan!" My pass got me into the building. How far can it get me?
brief.say: [eager] Send in my pilot, Kaplan! My pass got me into the building. How far can it get me?

scenes.hint: Lenny's token can read, not write: 403. Stu's can do both.

after.text: In under your name? Fine. But the exclamation mark stays.
after.say: [sulking] In under your name? Fine. But the exclamation mark stays.

brief.text: Retitle pilot 1 "Nothing Happens". It's version 1. Don't change what you haven't read.

scenes.hint: Four lines under the PATCH: who you are, what the body is, which version, and the change.

brief.text: Set pilot 1 to "picked up". Your retitle made it version 2. If I laugh, I'll sign it. I won't laugh.
brief.say: [flat, stern] Set pilot one to picked up. Your retitle made it version two. If I laugh, I'll sign it. [beat] I won't laugh.

scenes.hint: Stu's token, JSON, the version after the retitle, and the one field that changes.

outro.text: Mr. Pratt laughed. Once. A paramedic was called, to be safe. The network picked up six episodes.
Six episodes! Of nothing! We're geniuses!
outro.say: [ecstatic] Six episodes! Of nothing! We're geniuses!

outro.text: Same time next week, kid. Bring the cards.

request.title: Requests
request.text: The whole internet is people asking for things. A request is a method, what you want, and a path, what to. GET means give me. It answers: 200, OK. Like a waiter, but it never sighs.

path.title: Paths and ids
path.text: /orders is all the orders. /orders/7 is one of them, number 7. Ask for number 9 when there isn't one? 404 Not Found. The most famous number on the internet, and it means nothing. I relate.
path.say: Slash orders is all the orders. Slash orders slash seven is one of them, number seven. Ask for number nine when there isn't one? Four oh four, Not Found. The most famous number on the internet, and it means nothing. [beat] I relate.

post.title: POST
post.text: POST to a collection makes a new one in it. Send a body, and a Content-Type that says what it is. It says 201 Created, and Location: where it lives. More than Dana ever told me.

options.title: 405 and OPTIONS
options.text: Ask a path for something it doesn't do and it says 405, and tells you what it does do, in Allow. Or ask first, with OPTIONS. The only polite method. So naturally nobody uses it.

headers.title: Headers
headers.text: Under the first line go the headers. Name, colon, value. Accept says what you'll take back. Ask for what it hasn't got: 406 Not Acceptable. Leave it off, you get what's going. Like at my mother's.

contenttype.title: Content-Type
contenttype.text: Accept is what you want back. Content-Type is what you're sending. Send JSON and call it text? 415 Unsupported Media Type. You can't hand a man soup and call it a sandwich.

fields.title: 400 Bad Request
fields.text: The counter read it, and it's wrong. A field missing, or one it never asked for. 400 Bad Request. And the body tells you exactly what you did. Which is more than people do.

json.title: JSON
json.text: JSON is braces, keys and values. Every key is a string, and strings get double quotes. Not single. Not none. Who decided this? I'd like a word with him. In double quotes.

put.title: PUT
put.text: PUT goes to one thing's own path and replaces it. All of it: send every field. Send it twice, it's the same as once. Try that with POST and you've got two tables. Ask Lenny.

patch.title: PATCH
patch.text: PATCH changes part of a thing. Send only the fields that change, and the rest stays as it was. PUT is a new suit. PATCH is taking up the trousers.

delete.title: DELETE
delete.text: DELETE gets rid of a thing. And what does it send back? 204 No Content. It worked, and there's nothing to say about it. My favourite status. It's a show about nothing.

head.title: HEAD
head.text: HEAD is GET without the body. Same status, same headers, and then it just stops talking. You ask if something's there, and you don't hear all about it. If only people did this.

etag.title: ETags and 304
etag.text: An ETag is a version stamp. Send it back in If-None-Match: only if it's changed. Hasn't? 304 Not Modified, no body. Your browser never hears the same thing twice. My uncle should try it.

accepted.title: 202 Accepted
accepted.text: 201 means it's made. 202 means: we've got it, we'll get round to it. Not done, not refused. Accepted. It's "I'll call you" as a status code. The post office invented it.

ifmatch.title: If-Match
ifmatch.text: If-Match: change it only if it's still the version I saw. Changed since? 412 Precondition Failed. Also my last three relationships. And some counters won't change a thing without one: 428.

auth.title: Tokens
auth.text: Authorization: Bearer, then your token. Bearer! Very dramatic, for a password. No token, or one it doesn't know, and it's 401, with WWW-Authenticate telling you how to log in.

forbidden.title: 403 Forbidden
forbidden.text: 401 is: who are you? 403 is: I know exactly who you are, and no. It's the bouncer who remembers you. Logging in again won't help. Send someone who's allowed.

glossary.HEAD: GET, without the body
glossary.POST: make a new one in it
glossary.path: the path: what the request is about
glossary.If-None-Match: only if it's changed since this version
glossary.If-Match: only if it's still this version

wrong: It worked, but it's not what the scene wants. Look at what it did, and what was asked.
A 2, so it worked. Beautifully. On a completely different errand.
400: 400: the counter read it and didn't like it. The body says why. It went to the trouble, so read it.
401: 401: it doesn't know who you are. Nobody does, at first. It needs a token it knows.
403: 403: it knows exactly who you are, and the answer's no. Somebody else's token, maybe.
404: 404: nothing at that path. Check the path, and the id. Then check them again.
405: 405: that path doesn't do that. The Allow line says what it does. It's a menu. Read the menu.
406: 406: you asked for something it hasn't got. Look at your Accept. You don't ask a diner for sushi.
412: 412: it's changed since that version. Somebody got there first. Check the board.
415: 415: it can't read the body as what you said it was. Look at Content-Type. You called soup a sandwich.
428: 428: this counter won't change a thing without being told which version you saw.
par: Tight. Mr. Pratt almost moved his face.
over: It worked! There's a slip with fewer cards, though.
And scene. A card or two to spare, but it works.
It works. It rambles, but it works. Like my act.

errors.method: Every request needs a method. Put one on the slip.
errors.path: Every request needs a path. Put one on the slip.
errors.body: Only POST, PUT and PATCH carry a body here. fetch won't even send a GET with one.
